news.title: State Commander Recognizes Post 12248 for Exceeding Recruitment Goals
news.summary: Department of Maryland VFW Commander Todd A. Walter visited the Post's booth at the Calvert County Fair, praised its leadership, and made a $100 donation to the Post.
news.full:
Department of Maryland VFW Commander Todd A. Walter visited the Calvert County Fairgrounds during the 138th Calvert County Fair to meet with the leadership of the George W. Owings III VFW Post 12248 at the Post's booth, where he was welcomed by Commander Felix A. Figueroa, Senior Vice Commander Wayne Keller, and Adjutant Joseph Dixon. He thanked the Post for exceeding its recruitment goals for the year, praised its stellar representation throughout District 1, and presented a $100 donation to the Post.

Recognition from the State Commander is a meaningful milestone for any Post. For Post 12248, chartered just six months ago, it is a sign that a new Post can make a real difference quickly when its members show up for their community.

Exceeding a recruitment goal is about more than numbers. Every new member is a veteran who is now connected to fellow veterans, to the support of a local Post, and to help with the VA benefits and services they earned through their service. A strong membership also gives the VFW a louder voice when it speaks up for veterans in Annapolis and Washington, and a larger team of volunteers to serve veterans and families right here in Calvert County.

The Commander's donation will help the Post continue that work, supporting its outreach to local veterans and its service to the community.

The visit capped a busy week at the fair, where Post 12248 marched in the opening ceremony and welcomed veterans and families to its booth. Read more about the Post at the fair.

Not a member yet? If you served overseas in a war, campaign, or expedition, there is a place for you at Post 12248. Monthly meetings are held the 3rd Thursday of every month at 7:00 PM. Bring your DD-214, or learn how to join and send us a message.
news.caption: From left: Post 12248 Senior Vice Commander Wayne Keller; Department of Maryland VFW Commander Todd A. Walter; Post 12248 Commander Felix A. Figueroa; and Post 12248 Adjutant Joseph Dixon. Commander Walter stopped by the Calvert County Fairgrounds to visit Calvert County VFW Post 12248, thanking Post leadership for exceeding recruitment goals for the year, praising their stellar representation throughout District 1, and making a $100 donation to the George W. Owings III Post. (Photo courtesy of Felix A. Figueroa, VFW Post 12248 Commander)

news.title: Post 12248 Brings the VFW to the 138th Calvert County Fair
news.summary: Post leaders marched in the fair's opening ceremony, and the Post hosted a booth all five days to connect with veterans and families across Calvert County.
news.full:
For the first time, the George W. Owings III VFW Post 12248 took its place among the community organizations at the Calvert County Fair. Post leaders marched in the opening ceremony of the 138th fair in Prince Frederick, and the Post hosted a booth at the Calvert County Fairgrounds from Wednesday, September 30, through Sunday, October 4.

Few events bring Calvert County together the way the fair does. Among the thousands of families who walk the fairgrounds each year are many veterans who have never been part of a veterans organization, and some who have never been told about the benefits and support they earned through their service. Being at the fair gave Post 12248 the chance to meet those veterans where they are, in their own community.

That kind of outreach is at the heart of the VFW's mission. Many eligible veterans never join simply because no one has asked them. The booth gave veterans and their families a place to learn whether they qualify for VFW membership, find out how the Post can connect them with help on VA benefits, and meet the members who serve them in their own community.

The fair also showed the partnership between the veterans organizations of Chesapeake Beach. Commander Felix A. Figueroa marched alongside Post Chaplain Scott Deacon, who also serves as Commander of American Legion Stallings-Williams Post 206, and Adjutant Joseph Dixon. Post 206 hosted the ceremony where Post 12248 received its charter in March, and the two posts continue to work side by side for local veterans.

Just six months after its chartering, the Post is carrying forward the commitment of its namesake, Secretary George W. Owings III, to the men and women who wore our nation's uniform.

Missed us at the fair? It's not too late. Monthly meetings are held the 3rd Thursday of every month at 7:00 PM. Bring your DD-214, or learn how to join and send us a message.
news.caption: Calvert County’s VFW Post 12248 Commander Felix A. Figueroa (left), the post chaplain and American Legion Post 206 Commander Scott Deacon, and Adjutant Joseph Dixon take a quick selfie as they march during the opening ceremony of the 138th Calvert County Fair in Prince Frederick, MD. (Photo courtesy of Felix A. Figueroa, George W. Owings III VFW Post 12248 Commander)

news.title: Post 12248 officially chartered
news.summary: VFW Post 12248 received its charter in a ceremony at American Legion Stallings-Williams Post 206 in Chesapeake Beach.
news.full:
VFW Post 12248 was officially chartered on March 28, 2026, during a ceremony at American Legion Stallings-Williams Post 206 in Chesapeake Beach, Maryland.

The Post is dedicated to the memory of one of Chesapeake Beach's favorite sons, Secretary George W. Owings III. Read more about the Post and Secretary Owings.
